title: Tujia village - ethnic park near Zhangjiajie
text: Several ethnographic villages around Zhangjiajie showcase Tujia life - traditional stilt houses built without nails, hand-operated brocade looms, the bride crying ritual, sword dances and rice wine tastings. Evening shows with fire and music cost around 120-150 yuan.

title: Tujia and Miao - indigenous peoples of Zhangjiajie
text: Zhangjiajie is home to two ancient peoples: the Tujia (People of the Earth) known for sicin brocade weaving and drum dances, and the Miao famous for heavy silver jewelry and elaborate embroidery. Visit ethnic villages near the park or Fenghuang for deep cultural experiences.

title: How the floating mountains of Zhangjiajie formed
text: The quartzite sandstone pillars are 380 million years old. Once a shallow sea, sediment compacted into stone, then tectonic uplift exposed it. Wind, water and tree roots slowly carved out cracks, leaving 3,000+ freestanding pillars up to 400 m tall - unique on Earth.

title: Furong Town - the town with a waterfall
text: Furong is a small town 2 hours from Zhangjiajie where a 60-meter waterfall runs right through the center, with houses perched on cliffs above. Made famous by the 1986 film Hibiscus Town, it combines ancient stilt architecture, a 5 km riverside street and Tujia rice tofu.

title: Fenghuang - ancient town near Zhangjiajie
text: Fenghuang (Phoenix Ancient Town) is one of China's most beautiful old cities, just 4 hours by bus from Zhangjiajie. Wooden stilt houses line the Tuo River, with stone bridges, lanterns and narrow alleys that date back over 1,300 years. Stay overnight for magical river views.
